families.family: activations: unary elementwise (sigmoid, elu+1, logsigmoid/temperature, swish) fwd+bwd
families.reference: sigmoid: torch.sigmoid(x); elu_p1: F.elu(x) + 1; logsigmoid: F.logsigmoid(x) / temperature; swish: F.silu(x); bwd = autograd of each
spec_sources: fla/modules/activations/ops.py (elu_p1 has an inline torch fallback: torch.where(x>=0, x+1, x.clamp_max(0).exp()))
families.notes: Rows of any stride (row-strided [*, D] views); fp32 math, output in input dtype. temperature default 1.0. Pure elementwise; bwd kernels recompute from x.

families.family: activations: gated linear units (SwiGLU, SigmoidGLU, PowGLU) fwd + fused fwd/bwd
families.reference: swiglu: F.silu(x) * y; sigmoidglu: torch.sigmoid(x) * y; powglu: torch.where(x > 0, x.clamp_min(tiny) ** (power / (x.clamp_min(tiny).sqrt() + 1)) * torch.sigmoid(x), x * torch.sigmoid(x)) * y (power default 3.0); fwdbwd kernels = autograd (dx, dy) of these, optionally re-emitting z for the *_linear variants (F.linear done in torch)
spec_sources: PowGLUFunction docstring in fla/modules/activations/ops.py (Power Linear Unit, arXiv:2605.25704)
families.notes: PowGLU gate formula fixed by docstring: x^(p/(sqrt(x)+1))*sigmoid(x) for x>0 else swish; kernel feeds only x>0 lanes to log/sqrt. *_linear variants (SwiGLULinear etc.) fuse only the activation; the projection is F.linear in torch.

families.family: causal_conv1d (ShortConvolution) forward: depthwise causal conv + bias + optional silu + residual, varlen, initial state
families.reference: per sequence s (cu_seqlens segments, or batch rows): xs = x_s ([T_s, D]); prefix = h0[n, :, 1:].T if initial_state else zeros(W-1, D); xp = torch.cat([prefix, xs]).T[None]; y = F.conv1d(xp, weight[:, None, :], bias, groups=D)[0].T  (weight [D, W], y[t] = sum_i w[:, i] * x[t-W+1+i]); if activation in ('silu','swish'): y = F.silu(y); if residual: y = y + residual_s
spec_sources: Canon layers (residual variant) paper cited in docstring
families.notes: x [B,T,D] (any T/D strides), weight [D,W], initial_state [N,D,W] of which only slots 1..W-1 are read (slot W-1 = most recent token). weight=None means unweighted window sum. Residual added AFTER activation. Varlen: B==1, conv restarts per sequence. Gluon variant (opt-in FLA_GLUON / FLA_CONV_GLUON; W in {2,3,4}, no distributed, BlockedLayout only) has same semantics.

families.family: causal_conv1d backward (dx, dw, db, dh0, dresidual)
families.reference: autograd of the causal_conv1d forward reference w.r.t. x, weight, bias, initial_state (and residual = identity), including gradient flowing from final_state (dht) back into x / initial_state
families.notes: silu backward recomputes the pre-activation. dht path: final_state slots that still hold initial_state (T < W) pass gradient straight to dh0 (compute_dh0_kernel). Gluon bwd (opt-in) rejects state gradients and reduces dw/db partials in causal_conv1d_bwd_kernel_dwdb.

families.family: causal_conv1d final-state extraction and single-token decode update
families.reference: final_state[n] = torch.cat([h0[n] if initial_state else zeros(D, W), x_s.T], -1)[:, -W:]  (last W inputs, left-filled from initial_state then zeros); update: cache_new = torch.cat([cache[..., 1:], x[..., None]], -1); y = (cache_new * weight).sum(-1) + bias; y = F.silu(y) if silu; y = y + residual; cache updated in place
families.notes: Suspected deviation: causal_conv1d_update with cache=None never inserts x into the window (b_cache stays zero), so y = act(bias)+residual and x is ignored; with weight=None the wrapper fails (next_power_of_2(None)). Decode x may be [N,D], [1,N,D] or [N,1,D].

families.family: fused cross-entropy (per-row CE with label smoothing, logit scale, softcap, z-loss, ignore_index, vocab split/TP) fwd+bwd
families.reference: z = logits * logit_scale; z = c * torch.tanh(z / c) if softcap c else z; lse = torch.logsumexp(z, -1); valid = target != ignore_index; loss = F.cross_entropy(z, target, ignore_index=ignore_index, label_smoothing=ls, reduction='none') + valid * lse_square_scale * lse**2; z_loss = valid * lse_square_scale * lse**2 (non-differentiable, returned for logging); module reduction 'mean' = loss.sum() / valid.sum(), 'sum' = loss.sum(); dlogits = autograd of loss
families.notes: logits [N,V], target [N] global indices; label smoothing divides by total classes (V*world_size under process_group vocab sharding). Loss/lse fp32. inplace_backward overwrites logits with dlogits. Gluon backend opt-in (FLA_GLUON/FLA_CE_GLUON), BlockedLayout only; FLA_USE_FAST_OPS=1 switches to fast_expf/fast_logf.

families.family: fused linear cross-entropy (chunked F.linear + CE; grads precomputed in forward, scaled by upstream grad)
families.reference: logits = F.linear(x, weight, bias); loss = fused cross-entropy reference on logits with (ignore_index, label_smoothing, logit_scale, logit_softcapping), reduced by 'mean' (sum / max(#valid, 1)) or 'sum'; grads = autograd; elementwise_mul_kernel computes grad * do (scalar)
families.notes: The CE math runs through the fused_cross_entropy kernels; this file's own launched kernels are the grad scaler and logsumexp (separate family). use_l2warp=True adds the L2Wrap custom gradient (max-logit * l2_penalty_factor / N at the argmax of the raw logits) with no forward-loss term, i.e. not the autograd of the loss - reference must reproduce fla/modules/l2warp.py. 'mean' clamps #valid to >=1 (torch would give NaN when all ignored).

families.family: logsumexp over last dim (optional scale, optional tanh softcap)
families.reference: z = x * scale if scale else x; z = c * torch.tanh(z / c) if softcapping c else z; torch.logsumexp(z, dim=-1)
families.notes: Same kernel name in two files (utils version has no softcap). Kernel produces per-block partial lse [N, ceil(D/BD)], reduced with torch .logsumexp(-1). Output fp32 unless dtype given.

families.family: fused KL divergence (student/teacher linear + KL, batchmean) fwd+bwd
families.reference: F.kl_div(F.log_softmax(F.linear(x, weight), -1), F.log_softmax(F.linear(target_x, target_weight), -1), log_target=True, reduction='batchmean'); grads w.r.t. x, weight by autograd (teacher frozen); elementwise_mul_kernel scales precomputed grads by upstream scalar
families.notes: KL(teacher || student) per row summed over V, divided by N for batchmean (only reduction supported). Logit gradient (p_s - p_t)/N is written in place into the logits buffer in the logits dtype (not fp32). target_x/target_weight must not require grad.

families.reference: grpo_loss_torch in fla/modules/grpo/ops.py: logp = log_softmax(logits[:, :-1], -1).gather(-1, input_ids[:, -L:]); kl = exp(ref_logp - logp) - (ref_logp - logp) - 1; loss = -(exp(logp - logp.detach()) * advantages[:, None] - beta * kl) * completion_mask; save_kl also returns kl * mask; gradient = autograd
spec_sources: TRL GRPOTrainer loss (cited in file header)
families.notes: logits [B, L+1, V] (last position dropped, its grad zeroed), input_ids [B, K+L] (last L used), advantages [B], ref_logp [B,L]; masked tokens get loss 0 and zero grad. Forward value = beta*kl - advantage. inplace=True overwrites logits with grads.

families.family: layer_norm / rms_norm / group_norm with fused residual add (prenorm) fwd+bwd
families.reference: h = x + residual if residual is not None else x; LN: y = F.layer_norm(h, (D,), weight, bias, eps); RMS: y = F.rms_norm(h, (D,), weight, eps) + (bias if bias else 0); group (num_groups=G): hg = h.unflatten(-1, (G, D//G)); y = (F.layer_norm(hg, (D//G,), eps=eps) or F.rms_norm(hg, (D//G,), eps=eps)) * weight.view(G, -1) + bias.view(G, -1), flattened; prenorm returns (y, h); bwd = autograd (incl. dresidual passthrough)
families.notes: Biased variance, eps inside sqrt. weight/bias optional. residual add in fp32; residual_in_fp32 stores h in fp32. D <= 64KB/elem_size. *Linear variants (LayerNormLinear etc.) do F.linear in torch after the kernel.

families.family: gated layer/rms norm with group_size (Mamba2 RMSNormGated: norm(x*silu(z)) or norm(x)*silu(z)) fwd+bwd
families.reference: xg = x * F.silu(z) if (z is not None and not norm_before_gate) else x; grouped over last dim in chunks of group_size (default D): y = F.layer_norm(xg_group, (gs,), eps=eps) (or F.rms_norm) * weight_group + bias_group; if z is not None and norm_before_gate: y = y * F.silu(z); bwd = autograd
families.notes: Defaults differ per module: LayerNormGated norm_before_gate=True, RMSNormGated False. weight required (always loaded); bias optional.

families.family: fused norm + output gate (norm(x + residual) * act(g), act in swish/silu or sigmoid) fwd+bwd
families.reference: h = x + residual (if given); n = F.layer_norm(h, (D,), weight, bias, eps) or F.rms_norm(h, (D,), weight, eps) + bias; y = n * F.silu(g) (activation 'swish'/'silu') or n * torch.sigmoid(g) ('sigmoid'); prenorm returns (y, h); bwd = autograd w.r.t. x, g, weight, bias, residual
families.notes: Gate applied AFTER norm (unlike layernorm_gated's optional pre-norm gating). No group support (weight [D]). Kernel silently applies no gate for an unknown activation string; modules reject it.

families.family: layer/rms norm + BitNet int8 absmax activation fake-quant (fused BitLinear front-end) fwd+bwd
families.reference: h = x + residual; n = F.layer_norm(h,(D,),w,b,eps) or F.rms_norm(h,(D,),w,eps)(+b); s = 127 / n.abs().amax(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-5); q = (n * s).round().clamp(-128, 127) / s; y = n + (q - n).detach()  (straight-through estimator, as in fla/modules/fused_bitlinear.py BitLinear); bwd = autograd of that (STE: quant has identity gradient)
families.notes: Deviation: kernel rounds half AWAY from zero (floor(x+0.5)/ceil(x-0.5), comment: triton-ascend lacks libdevice.round) while the repo's torch reference uses torch.round (half-to-even) -> differs at exact .5 ties. Weight 1.58-bit quant and F.linear are done in torch.

families.reference: y = x * torch.rsqrt((x * x).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + eps)  (eps default 1e-6); bwd = autograd
families.notes: NOT F.normalize: eps is added to the squared norm inside the sqrt (F.normalize uses max(||x||, eps)). Backward uses saved y and rstd: dx = rstd*(dy - (dy.y) y), exact autograd. D <= 64KB/elem_size.

families.family: rotary embedding (non-interleaved / interleaved, partial rotary dim, seqlen offsets, varlen) fwd+bwd
families.reference: rotary_embedding_ref(x, cos[pos], sin[pos], interleaved) from fla/modules/rotary/ops.py: x[..., :2R]*cos_rep + rotate_half(x[..., :2R], interleaved)*sin_rep, x[..., 2R:] unchanged, with pos = t (position within each sequence; restarts at 0 per cu_seqlens segment) + seqlen_offsets (int or per-sequence [N]); bwd = same op with sin negated (conjugate=True)
families.notes: x [B,T,H,D], cos/sin [TR, R] (rotary dim 2R <= D <= 256), dtypes must match x. Positions with pos<0 or >=TR (left-padding via negative offsets) are left ZERO in the rotated part when not inplace (unchanged when inplace) - a code-visible convention.

families.family: token shift (delta = x[t-1] - x[t], zero/cache for first token, varlen, decode cache) fwd+bwd
families.reference: token_shift_ref in fla/modules/token_shift.py: per sequence, shifted = F.pad(x_s, (0,0,1,0))[:-1] with shifted[0] = cache[n] if cache else 0; y = shifted - x_s; cache_out[n] = x_s[-1]; bwd = autograd (incl. grad to cache)
families.notes: x [B,T,D]; varlen requires B==1; cache [N,D]. Bwd kernels also handle grad_cache_in from a next context-parallel rank.

families.family: chunk-local and global cumsum (scalar [B,T,H] / vector [B,T,H,S], reverse, scale, varlen)
families.reference: global: o = scale * torch.cumsum(s, dim=1) per sequence (reverse: flip-cumsum-flip); local: split each sequence's time axis into consecutive chunks of chunk_size starting at the sequence start, o = scale * cumsum within each chunk (reverse: suffix sums within chunk); scale defaults to 1
families.notes: Layout [B,T,H(,S)], fp32 accumulation, output_dtype default fp32. chunk_size must be a power of 2. Varlen: B==1 + cu_seqlens; chunks restart at each sequence start. Used by many attention ops with scale=1/ln2 (log2-space gates).

families.family: solve_tril: per-chunk inverse (I + A)^-1 of strictly-lower-triangular A (16/32/64 blocks)
families.reference: for each chunk of BT rows (BT = A.shape[-1] in {16,32,64}; chunks restart per sequence) and head: M = torch.tril(A_chunk[:, :L], -1) (L = valid rows in chunk); Ai_chunk = torch.linalg.solve_triangular(torch.eye(L) + M, torch.eye(L), upper=False) (== torch.linalg.inv(I + M)); entries above the diagonal and rows/cols beyond T are 0
families.notes: A [B,T,H,BT]; diagonal and upper part of A are ignored (masked). Output dtype fp32 by default. Optional TMA path (FLA_USE_TMA=1 and cc>=9) and tf32 dot precision (FLA_TRIL_PRECISION) are off on sm86; default ieee dots.

families.reference: torch.softmax(x, dim=-1); bwd: autograd (ds = p * (dp - (p * dp).sum(-1, keepdim=True)))
families.notes: Output dtype fp32 by default; whole row in one block (D up to next_pow2).

families.family: logcumsumexp along time (used by ABC chunk)
families.reference: torch.logcumsumexp(s, dim=1) for s laid out [B*H, T, S]
families.notes: Suspected deviation: in the last partial block, padded rows are loaded as 0.0 (not -inf) and enter the running max, so if valid values are << 0 the exp underflows and the result is clamped to log(1e-20)+max; any within-block range > ~88 also hits the 1e-20 clamp. Launched from fla/ops/abc/chunk.py.

families.reference: matmul(a, b, activation): act(a @ b) with act in {'' (none), 'relu': F.relu, 'leaky_relu': F.leaky_relu(.,0.01), 'sigmoid': torch.sigmoid, 'tanh': torch.tanh}; addmm(x, a, b, alpha, beta): alpha*(a @ b) + beta*x (x broadcast as [N] bias or [M,N]); a 2D or batched 3D, b 2D
families.notes: Not used inside fla. tanh is implemented as (e^x-e^-x)/(e^x+e^-x) -> NaN for |x| > ~88 (fp32 exp overflow). alpha/beta are read with tl.load, so they must be passed as 1-element tensors despite the float type hint. tf32 allowed for non-fp32 inputs.

families.family: pack / unpack padded sequences (left or right padding) via cu_seqlens
families.reference: pack: torch.cat([x[b, S - L_b:] if padding_side == 'left' else x[b, :L_b] for b in range(B)]) with L_b = diff(cu_seqlens); unpack: inverse scatter into zeros([N, S, ...]); bwd of each = the other
families.notes: Pure data movement; default padding_side='left'.

families.family: chunk mean pooling over time (fixed chunk_size, varlen) fwd+bwd
families.reference: per sequence, split time into consecutive chunks of chunk_size from the sequence start; o[c] = x[chunk c].mean(dim=time) (last partial chunk averaged over its actual length); output [B, NT, H, D] (varlen: [1, total_chunks, H, D]); bwd = autograd
families.notes: Layout [B,T,H,D]; fp32 accumulation. Used by NSA-style compression.

families.family: block-selection to CSR inversion (NSA backward helper)
families.reference: valid = (slot < block_counts) & (0 <= idx < num_blocks) & (idx*block_size <= t); block_id = (b*H + h)*num_blocks + idx (dense) or (chunk_offsets[seq(t)] + idx)*H + h (varlen); csr_offsets = cat([0], torch.bincount(block_id[valid], minlength=NB).cumsum(0)); csr_indices[:nnz] = (b*T + t)[valid] grouped by block_id (e.g. stable argsort)
families.notes: Integer op. Order of query indices within a block is nondeterministic (atomic scatter): compare per-block as multisets. csr_indices is over-allocated to B*T*H*S. Docstring mentions a radix-sort path for long problems that the code does not have.

families.family: fused beta sigmoid gate (beta = scale * sigmoid(x), used by gated delta rule) fwd+bwd
families.reference: y = scale * torch.sigmoid(x) (scale = 2.0 when allow_neg_eigval else 1.0 in gated_delta_rule); bwd = autograd
families.notes: Output fp32 regardless of input dtype; flat elementwise.

families.reference: same as the CUDA activation families (torch.sigmoid, F.logsigmoid/T, F.silu, F.silu(x)*y, PowGLU formula); bwd = autograd
families.notes: Triton-Ascend backend, dispatched only when IS_NPU (Huawei Ascend).

families.family: [Ascend] causal_conv1d (fwd, bwd, dh0, final states, decode update)
families.reference: same as CUDA causal_conv1d forward / backward / states+update families
families.notes: NPU-only dispatch; uses Ascend-only builtins (tl.extract_slice/insert_slice / extra.cann).

families.family: [Ascend] fused losses (cross-entropy, linear cross-entropy, KL div, GRPO)
families.reference: same as the CUDA fused cross-entropy / linear cross-entropy / KL / GRPO families
families.notes: NPU-only dispatch. elementwise_mul_kernel exists in both the FLCE and KL Ascend files. Ascend FLCE fuses CE fwd+grad in cross_entropy_kernel; multi-rank process groups unsupported on Ascend.

families.reference: same as CUDA layer_norm/rms_norm(+residual), fused norm-gate, and l2norm (x*rsqrt(sum x^2 + eps)) families
families.notes: NPU-only dispatch (registered for layer_norm_fwd/bwd, layer_norm_gated_fwd/bwd, l2norm_fwd/bwd).

families.reference: same as CUDA rotary family (rotary_embedding_ref)
families.notes: NPU-only dispatch.

families.family: [Ascend] ops/utils helpers (chunk local/global cumsum, solve_tril, fused beta sigmoid)
families.reference: same as CUDA chunk cumsum, solve_tril ((I+tril(A,-1))^-1 per chunk) and fused beta sigmoid families
families.notes: NPU-only dispatch via the triton_ascend backend registry.
